nodes.name: Read Lead State
nodes.notes:
Read HERE, milliseconds before the send, and not trusted from whatever the caller
was holding. The caller may have decided to send this message hours ago; the only
state that matters is the state now.

nodes.name: Read Job State
nodes.notes:
EDGE CASE 10, the last link in it. The tick claims a job and calls this workflow;
between those two moments an opt-out can arrive and cancel the job. Re-reading the
job row here closes that window. The sentinel keeps the query from matching
anything when the caller is not a queued job at all.

nodes.name: Send Email
nodes.notes:
Plain text, and appendAttribution off. A prospect-facing message that arrives
with an automation tool's footer on it announces that nobody read their enquiry.

nodes.name: Send WhatsApp

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ messaging_product: 'whatsapp', to: $('Stop Conditions').first().json.to, type: 'text', text: { body: $('Stop Conditions').first().json.body } }) }}

nodes.notes:
The request body is the real WhatsApp Business Cloud API shape, and the mock
answers with the real response shape (messages[0].id = a wamid). Swapping to Meta
is this URL and a credential - no code below this node changes, because it reads
the provider id out of the same field either way.

nodes.name: Skipped
nodes.notes:
A suppressed send is a SUCCESS, not a failure - the system did exactly what it
should. Returning it as an error would fill the dead-letter queue with correct
behaviour and train whoever reads it to ignore the queue.

nodes.name: Write Send Audit

value.detail_json: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channel: $json.channel, template: $json.template, step: $json.step, audience: $json.audience, intended_to: $json.intended_to, actual_to: $json.to, redirected: $json.redirected, provider_ref: $json.provider_ref || "", reason: $json.reason || "", error: $json.error || "" }) }}

nodes.notes:
Both outcomes are logged with the same weight. "Why did this lead never hear from
us" is asked far more often than "why did they", and it is only answerable if the
suppressions were written down too.

parameters.content:
## LP-92 Send Message

**Every outbound message in the system goes through this one workflow**, which is what makes the guarantees below statable at all.

**Claim -> send -> complete**, keyed `message:<lead>:<template>:<step>`. A retried caller, a replayed dead letter and a double-fired tick all produce one message. **(EC-8)**

**Stop conditions are re-read HERE**, milliseconds before the send: consent, lead status, approval state, and the job row itself. An opt-out at 10:59 stops the 11:00 follow-up. **(EC-10, EC-12)**

**`demo_redirect_email` in `lp_config`** sends every lead-facing message to one inbox with the intended recipient in the subject. A staging system that can reach a real prospect is one typo away from an incident. Manager alerts are never redirected.
